One more consideration: the user premise "developers assume the same propagation will happen whenever the database crashes and the container runtime restarts it" — the services reference explicitly says restart: true excludes automated restart by the container runtime after the container dies. Good.

Also "Can this configuration alone justify promising that the API remains ready to serve throughout later database failures?" — No: depends_on only orders startup; nothing restarts/heals API after runtime failure of db; no retry/backoff guarantee; healthcheck-dependent restart propagation is not a documented feature. Also if the API container itself is running but its DB connections fail, no Compose mechanism restarts it. Mark as documented limitation.

Migration: use separate one-shot service with depends_on db: condition: service_healthy, and API depends_on migration: condition: service_completed_successfully. Also note: a service that exits successfully — if restarted by explicit Compose restart of db with restart:true from migration? Careful: `restart: true` on API's dependency on migration would restart API when the migration service is updated/restarted. But the migration service completing successfully and restarting it makes it run again — that's the standard pattern.

Also important: `service_completed_successfully` requires that the dependency service be a one-shot; if the migration container exits 0, Compose treats it as satisfied. Also note that if migration service has a restart policy of always, it would loop — recommendation: no restart policy for migration (default "no") or "on-failure"? Keep as default no; exit code must be 0.

Also for `docker compose up`, if migration service is already exited-0 from previous run, Compose may not re-run it unless recreated... Actually known behavior: `service_completed_successfully` waits for the dependency container to have exited with 0; on subsequent `up`, if the container exists as exited 0, it's considered satisfied. Hmm, need doc support. The docs "Compose guarantees dependency services marked with service_completed_successfully completed successfully before starting a dependent service." Not much more. I could mark UNVERIFIED about whether a previously completed migration container is re-run on subsequent `up`.

Also the API's short-form depends_on: change to long syntax to add condition and restart. Note that short form gives only service_started ("Compose does not wait for dependency services to be 'healthy'"). So replacing short-form is necessary for health gating.

Also the restart:true nuance: "Compose restarts this service after it updates the dependency service. This applies to an explicit restart controlled by a Compose operation". Actually the phrase in services ref: "When set to true Compose restarts this service after it updates the dependency service. This applies to an explicit restart controlled by a Compose operation, and excludes automated restart by the container runtime after the container dies." And startup-order page: "restart: true ensures that if db is updated or restarted due to an explicit Compose operation, for example docker compose restart, the web service is also restarted automatically". Good.

Also, does the API need `restart: unless-stopped`/`always` for itself? That's about its own crash handling, not dependency.

Healthcheck for the API itself would be needed for readiness but Compose doesn't act on it for dependents except at dependency startup. "Docker Compose does not wait until a container is 'ready', only until it's running" — actually the doc says "Compose does not wait until a container is 'ready'". Hmm, it says "On startup, Compose does not wait until a container is 'ready', only until it's running." Then describes service_healthy solution.

Also relevant: `docker compose restart` — does it restart dependents by default? The startup-order docs say restart:true ensures dependent restart on explicit Compose operation. Without restart:true, dependents are not restarted. That supports the statement that explicit restart propagation requires restart: true (available in 2.17.0, so 2.18.0 supports it).

Also `required: false` introduced in 2.20.0 per services reference — so with 2.18.0 declaring `required: false` under depends_on is not supported. What happens?
